entries.title: Ezekiel 34:1
segments: "The shepherds of Israel" spoken of in this chapter, are all their rulers and guides, as well in political as in religious matters.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:2
segments:
vv 2-3. 
 
It is the business of rulers and religious teachers to seek the welfare of those committed to their care, not their own pleasure and emolument. They who use the holy office of the ministry as a means of advancing their worldly interests, and are more anxious to find good places for themselves than to "feed the flock of God," are hirelings, and not true shepherds.  God will be against them, and will give their work to others who will perform it faithfully,

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:4
segments: Christ's ministers ought, after the example of their great Master, to bestow special labor upon "men of low degree," carefully seeking out the poor and friendless, the feeble-minded, the ignorant, and the erring; remembering in all their ministrations that Christ has sent them "to seek and save that which was lost."

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:5
segments:
vv 5-6. 
 
When pastors are unfaithful, "seeking their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's," their flocks are soon scattered, a prey to the destroyer.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:7
segments:
vv 7-22. 
 
God will see that his church is provided with faithful shepherds.  If those whom he has set over her neglect their work, and seek their own pleasure, profit, or honor, he will take from them the kingdom of heaven, and give it to pastors after his own heart.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:10
segments: Require my flock at their hand; call them to an account for its destruction.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:17
segments: I judge--he-goats; more exactly, I judge cattle against cattle, against rams and he-goats; I judge and protect the lean cattle against the fat cattle; namely, against the rams and he-gaots: that is, I defend my humble worshippers against their proud oppressors.  See

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:23
segments: One Shepherd--my servant David; the Messiah, who is "the good shepherd,"

. 
 
vv 23-24. 
 
The Lord Jesus is the great Shepherd and Prince of the churches.  From him alone all the under-shepherds receive grace to perform their sacred office aright; and to him alone must his people look, in times of declension and destitution, for a supply of faithful pastors.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:25
segments:
vv 25-31. 
 
Whatever may be the general state of Christ's church, he supplies all the wants of those who make him the Shepherd and Bishop of their souls; defends them from every enemy, makes all their trials work together for their good, and finally gathers them into his heavenly fold, where they shall no more hunger or thirst for ever.  He will in due time extend his church universal over all the earth, and fill all nations, through her, with light and peace and blessedness.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:29
segments: A Plant of renown; the same as "a righteous Branch,"
; that is, the Messiah.  The fulfilment of the promises recorded in this chapter extends through the whole history of the true church to the end of time.
